html:
A nationwide uprising for democracy in Burma in 1988, named for its great general strike on 8 August 1988 (8.8.88). The army crushed it in September.

General Ne Win had ruled since a coup in 1962. By the late 1980s the economy had collapsed. In 1987 the government cancelled most banknotes without warning, wiping out people's savings, and Burma was listed by the United Nations as one of the world's poorest countries.

Student protests in Rangoon in March 1988 were met with killings. In July Ne Win resigned, warning that if the army shot, it would shoot to hit. On 8 August millions marched across the country. Soldiers fired on crowds, killing thousands over the following weeks. Late in August, Aung San Suu Kyi spoke to a vast crowd at the Shwedagon Pagoda and became the leader of the movement.

On 18 September the army seized power directly. The new junta renamed the country Myanmar and held elections in 1990, which the National League for Democracy won and the generals then ignored.
sum: A nationwide uprising for democracy in Burma in 1988, named for its great general strike on 8 August 1988 (8.8.88). The army crushed it in September.
